newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL palm oil ends up despite profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: KL palm oil ends up despite profit-taking.

text.p: PALM OIL FUTURES PALM OIL PHYSICAL

PALM OIL FUTURES - Underlying bullish fundamentals and gains in the Chicago soyoil futures pushed the market higher. Prices, however, closed with smaller gains due to profit-taking. Trend was unclear as players returned from year-end holidays. March futures support - 1,240/resistance - 1,265.
PALM OIL PHYSICAL - Also saw scattered dealings and more fresh interest is expected next week.
SGS said that export in December was estimated to be around 717,197 tonnes and Caleb Brett at 702,082 tonnes against its estimate of 673,905 for November.
Traders had estimated output in December would fall by up to 18 percent over the previous month, and also expect a lower end-December stock level of below 900,000 tonnes.
"We feel that stocks for end-year should be around 850,000 to 870,000 tonnes," another trader said.
"There was good buying above the 1,250 ringgit level and people are feeling more confident," he said.
At the close, March futures contract was seven ringgit up at 1,254 ringgit ($496.83) a tonne after trading between 1,249 and 1,260.
Traders said the next resistance will be at 1,265 ringgit with strong support seen at 1,240.
Among physical, Jan (south) saw offers at 1,300 ringgit against bids at 1,295, after trading from 1,295 to 1,300.

Jan (north) was offered at 1,285 and bids at 1,277.50. Feb (south) saw offers at 1,300 with bids at 1,295, with earlier trades at 1,295 and 1,297.50. Feb (central) was offered at 1,285 and bid at 1,275.
